en: Mature Experience

The Guru, from whom the web of duality has fallen away through the most mature of his own direct experiences, [taught] that which is hidden to those of wicked intellect burdened by a multitude of sins, yet is manifest to those endowed with wisdom.
Although that Truth was perfectly realized within his own heart, he recalled it for the sake of awakening his excellent disciples, by means of his own vision of the entire world. 1.

This entire world that has arisen within me as duality is false, constructed by the mind; it is not established by anything other than delusion, like water imagined in a mirage upon the wind-swept desert where no water exists.
If indeed this entire visible world does not exist, nor do I, then I am pure, I am indivisible, my body being composed solely of the essence of mature bliss and consciousness. || 2 ||

This insentient body is not I; it is certain that I am not like a wall or similar objects. Nor am I the vital breath (prāṇamaya), which is like air held within a leather bag; that is certain. I am not even the mind-made (manomaya) one, which is as fickle as a monkey and corrupted by miserliness.
Intellect, like the conduct of a Buddha, is merely hypocrisy; it is not ignorance, which is a darkness devoid of light.

I am not even like the Khadira tree, for I am eternally distinct from those things that shine in the sky through their resemblance to water; I am invisible, like the solar light which is devoid of contact with visible objects and is, like the sky, of a pervasive nature. According to the true state of reality, I am like the ocean to these waves and the like. || 4 ||
I am non-dual; I am the stainless sky of consciousness; I am full; I am bodiless; I am without senses; I am utterly devoid of the category of vital breaths;
I am one whose mind is liberated from impurity; I am the treasury of overflowing wisdom.
I am free from illusion, I am without end, and I am the vast, mature, and radiant light.
Indeed, there is nothing other than Me; if anything appears as an object of consciousness, it is false, like the fire in a gem. I am the substratum for all conceptualization.
I am the Seer of all, I am the state of equal flavor (samarasa), I am tranquil, I am sinless, I am full,
I am devoid of duality, I am the vast space, and I am eternal. In me, who am this ultimate reality, knowable through the crest of the Vedas, there is self-luminosity.
Or what contradiction could there be? For all this shines forth indeed through his presence.
Seeing everything perceived through the power of the sun’s light, people have no doubt regarding it; therefore, I am some unique radiance, the absolute Śiva.
I am of the nature of eternal manifestation; I am the pure, eternal sky; I am the peaceful one; I am composed of eternal bliss; I am he from whom the great darkness of delusion has departed.

I have realized the entire reality of the ultimate truth, which is innate, free from all impurity, attainable by the liberated, and devoid of the conceptualization of duality; I am that which is designated as absolute liberation (kaivalya). || 8 ||

"Just as duality in a dream is unreal, so too the duality of the waking state is merely mental and false; having abandoned this, I am of the singular nature of the pure, conscious, and stainless Self."

Or rather, having realized that this entire object of knowledge is incessantly my very own form, I remain as one who has abandoned [all else], profound and deep like the great ocean when its winds have subsided. || 9 ||
What is there to go to here, for me whose form is entirely complete and unbroken; what duty remains here, for me whose body is actionless and whose sole nature is liberation?
For one who is non-dual, there is nothing else to be abandoned, nor is there any other goal to be attained;
today I am at peace, liberated and stainless like a cloud free from water.
What have we gained from before this, and what have we now obtained through investigation and the like,
since I am constantly ablaze as that very nature of bliss?

Or rather, what need is there here even for me to consider false deliberations and the like, since I am beyond duality and non-duality, established in the single flavor where supreme silence is the consensus? 11.
What is there for me, who am full of right vision, to hear, since I am free from false perception?
And what is there for me, who am the light beyond doubt, to think at all?
For me, whose form is the destruction of the distinction between meditator and object of meditation, there is no object of meditation at all;
nor indeed is there any "meditative absorption" for me, who am the constant, singular great essence of the Self of all. 12.

Even the discrimination between self and non-self does not please me as formulated by the learned, since there is no such thing as a "non-self" that exists; for what objectified form could possibly be capable of being discriminated?

Alas, those whose nature is unseen engage in the investigation and contemplation of false speech; they are not even brothers [to truth], for those of firm intellect remain silent, established like stones. ||13||

In accordance with the true state of reality, oh, I am some indeterminate entity; yet I do not appear as anything at all, being beyond the reach of continuous perception and outside the domain of speech and mind.
I am sinless, I am fearless, I am free from the stain of even the slightest doubt; I am the great, mature radiance of peace, incomparable and cool. || 14 ||
I, who was previously pure through the cessation of all mental constructs, am awakened; for from me this world arose, and it is sustained by me.

Salutations to that one who is always of the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss; who is vast wisdom; and into whom fear itself dissolves upon reaching dissolution, for he is without any further substratum. 15.
There exists that which is of the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss, eternally; know this, O friend: neither "I" nor "you" is false, nor is this entire perceived world non-existent.
That which was spoken by me to you out of compassion is the truth; believe this clearly, O sinless one, if you possess a pure intellect—let there be no doubt for you. (16)

This [teaching], which possesses its own natural elegance and is easily understood by a beautiful mind, should be given to one who has mature experience; it must not be given to one whose intellect is like milk mixed with poison, nor to one who is wicked at heart.
This very [teaching], having reached the head of the most excellent ones adorned with lovely wisdom, shines forth of its own accord.
If that ketaki flower were to fall into the reach of a monkey's hand, would it shine? || 17 ||
Thus ends the *Prauḍhānubhūti*.
